text.description: Gather, split, dry, or carry fuel for household use.

text.label: Make herbal preparations for personal use
text.description: Make plant- or herb-based preparations for personal use.

text.label: Hunt or trap for personal use
text.description: Hunt, trap, or gather animal products for personal use.

text.label: Make metal goods for personal use
text.description: Work metal and make metal goods or tools for personal use.

text.label: Extract materials for personal use
text.description: Extract or collect minerals, stone, sand, clay, or similar materials for personal use.

text.label: Make goods from other materials for personal use
text.description: Make goods from materials not covered by a more specific own-use category.

text.label: Build or substantially renovate for personal use
text.description: Build or substantially renovate a home, structure, or infrastructure for personal use.

text.label: Prepare supplies and materials for personal production
text.description: Buy or prepare raw materials and manage the results of personal production.

text.label: Make textiles, clothing, or leather goods for personal use
text.description: Make or process textiles, clothing, leather, or footwear for personal use.

text.label: Collect water from a source for personal use
text.description: Collect, draw, or carry water for personal use.

text.label: Gather wild foods or useful plants for personal use
text.description: Gather wild edible or useful products for personal use.

text.label: Make wood or bark items for personal use
text.description: Make objects or prepared materials from wood or bark for personal use.

text.label: Pack a meal or snack to take with you
text.description: Pack a meal or snack for yourself or your household.

text.label: Pack or unpack and restore order at home
aliases: Put things away after a move
text.description: Pack or unpack belongings and put the home back in order after a trip, move, or household change.

text.label: Organize a move and household belongings
text.description: Plan a move and sort belongings to decide what to keep, store, give away, sell, or discard.

text.label: Pay household bills
text.description: Review and pay utility or household bills.

text.label: Care for a pet
text.description: Feed, care for, walk, or maintain a pet’s living environment.

text.label: Provide daily care for a pet
text.description: Feed or water a pet, wash its bowls, clean its space or litter, bathe it, or handle everyday grooming.

text.label: Provide other care for a pet
aliases: Keep an eye on an animal
text.description: Do another pet-care task not covered by daily care or a service.

text.label: Arrange or attend a veterinary or other pet service
text.description: Arrange or receive veterinary, grooming, boarding, day-care, or another service for a pet.

text.label: Plan household tasks and schedules
text.description: Plan household tasks, schedules, supplies, home services, and who will do what.

text.label: Care for ornamental plants or outdoor areas
text.description: Water, trim, or weed indoor and ornamental plants, the lawn, yard, or landscape.

text.label: Prepare tea or coffee at home
text.description: Prepare a homemade drink as a separate household activity if you want to track it.

text.label: Preserve or store a harvest
text.description: Preserve, can, dry, freeze, or ferment a harvest or food for future use.

text.label: Reheat food or assemble a simple meal
text.description: Reheat food or put together a simple meal at home.

text.label: Oversee a repair to furniture, an appliance, or a computer
text.description: Stay with, explain, or check a repair to furniture, toys, appliances, or a computer.

text.label: Oversee a home repair or construction job
text.description: Stay on site, check, or coordinate home repair, construction, or maintenance without doing the repair work yourself.

text.label: Hang up or collect laundry to dry
text.description: Hang laundry to dry or take it down, or use a dryer and collect the laundry afterward.

text.label: Hang, take down, and collect laundry
text.description: Hang up or take down laundry and collect dry clothing or textiles.

text.label: Iron and fold laundry
text.description: Iron, fold, and put away clean clothing and textiles.

text.label: Mend clothing or care for shoes
text.description: Darn or hem clothing, repair garments, or clean and polish shoes.

text.label: Care for clothing, shoes, or household textiles in another way
text.description: Do another clothing, footwear, bedding, or household-textile care task.

text.label: Put away clothing and household textiles
text.description: Put folded or clean clothing and textiles away.

text.label: Sort clothing and laundry
text.description: Sort clothing or household textiles before washing or storage.

text.label: Wash clothing and household textiles
text.description: Sort, load, and wash clothing, bedding, curtains, and household textiles.

text.label: Maintain or repair a personal vehicle
text.description: Clean, lubricate, service, or repair a personal or family car, motorcycle, bicycle, or other vehicle.

text.label: Prepare a personal vehicle for the season
aliases: Prepare a car for the season
text.description: Clean, lubricate, service, or prepare a personal vehicle for the season.

text.label: Wait for a utility or home service without doing another task
text.description: Set aside time to wait for gas, water, waste collection, a delivery, or another service when you are not tracking a parallel active task.

text.label: Handle the active steps of laundry, excluding machine run time
text.description: Sort, load, start, unload, or move laundry. The machine’s unattended run time is not a human activity if you are doing something else.

text.label: Sort or take out household waste
text.description: Take out trash, sort recyclables, or dispose of unwanted household items.

text.label: Maintain a household water supply
text.description: Maintain a household water system such as a well, pump, tank, or domestic supply.

text.label: Prepare the home for a season or severe weather
aliases: Prepare the home for bad weather
text.description: Get the home, yard, or household systems ready for a seasonal change or severe weather.

text.label: Gather wild mushrooms, berries, or other foods
text.description: Look for and gather mushrooms, berries, or other wild foods for the household.

text.label: Make useful household items from wood
text.description: Work with wood or bark to make tools, dishes, or other items for the home.

text.label: Create expressive work through code
text.description: Use code as an expressive medium for visual, audio, or interactive work.

text.label: Build an interactive prototype
text.description: Create an interactive prototype of a website, app, installation, or other digital artifact.

text.label: Administer accounts and access
text.description: Manage system accounts, groups, licenses, and access permissions.

text.label: Configure or test backup and restore
text.description: Set up backups or verify that data and systems can be restored from them.

text.label: Design or configure cloud infrastructure
text.description: Design or configure cloud resources, containers, and environments.

text.label: Defend systems against cybersecurity threats
text.description: Investigate security events, harden systems, and monitor vulnerabilities and security policies.

text.label: Build and operate data pipelines
text.description: Create pipelines to ingest, transform, store, or transfer datasets, including ELT or ETL workflows.

text.label: Administer databases and data stores
text.description: Manage database permissions, backups, configuration, and performance.

text.label: Repair or configure computer and network equipment
aliases: Repair a computer or network device
text.description: Repair or configure computing devices or networking equipment.

text.label: Resolve a user’s technical support request
text.description: Diagnose a user’s issue and work through the technical support request to resolution.

text.label: Install and configure an IT system
aliases: Set up a network or service
text.description: Install or configure a device, application, network, or service.

text.label: Operate and maintain machine-learning systems
aliases: Deploy and monitor an ML system
text.description: Deploy, monitor, or retrain machine-learning systems as operational services.

text.label: Configure or troubleshoot a network
text.description: Configure or diagnose a business or home network.

text.label: Monitor systems, logs, and alerts
text.description: Monitor system health, network logs, and alerts for operational issues.

text.label: Practice a language through conversation
text.description: Practice a chosen language in spoken conversation or dialogue with another person.

text.label: Take part in a language exchange conversation
aliases: Practice a language with a partner
text.description: Have a conversation in a language you are learning with a partner, teacher, or other conversation partner. Solo speaking, pronunciation drills, and repeating a recording are separate activities; choose the partner role and communication channel when relevant.

text.label: Review corrections and analyze language mistakes
text.description: Review corrections and examine your own mistakes while learning a language.

text.label: Practice dictation or transcription by ear
text.description: Write down spoken material from listening practice, or transcribe it by ear.

text.label: Have a language on in the background
text.description: Listen to or watch language content passively; track it separately only if you explicitly want background exposure counted.

text.label: Review language flashcards
text.description: Use flashcards or recall exercises to review words, phrases, and other language material.

text.label: Study grammar or do grammar exercises
text.description: Study grammar concepts or complete grammar-focused exercises.

text.label: Practice a language with media
aliases: Watch or listen for language practice
text.description: Watch or listen to content in the language you are learning when you are intentionally using it as language practice.

text.label: Attend a language lesson
text.description: Study a language in a lesson with a teacher, in a group, or through a structured lesson plan.

text.label: Listen for overall meaning
text.description: Listen to authentic or graded content mainly to understand the gist and build comprehension.

text.label: Study a short audio clip closely
aliases: Replay and analyze a short clip
text.description: Listen to a short piece with pauses, analysis, or repeated listening.

text.label: Practice a language
text.description: Intentionally practice a language through reading, writing, listening, speaking, or exercises.

text.label: Practice pronunciation and speech sounds
text.description: Work on speech sounds, prosody, and pronunciation.

text.label: Read for practice and overall understanding
text.description: Read to practice a language and understand the general meaning of a text.

text.label: Analyze a text in detail
aliases: Study words and grammar in a text
text.description: Study a text closely, including its vocabulary and grammar.

text.label: Repeat spoken language in sync or phrase by phrase
text.description: Repeat speech along with a recording or one phrase at a time; keep this distinct from general listening or speaking practice.

text.label: Practice speaking on your own
text.description: Practice spoken output through a monologue, story, or self-directed conversation.

text.label: Do a translation exercise for language study
text.description: Translate as a learning exercise rather than as a separate translation service task.

text.label: Study or review vocabulary
text.description: Learn or review words, phrases, and flashcards.

text.label: Write to practice a language
aliases: Write in a language you are learning
text.description: Write independently as practice in the language you are learning.

text.label: Learn through an apprenticeship or work placement
text.description: Learn as part of an apprenticeship or work-based placement; a role or status axis can add detail when useful.

text.label: Build a portfolio or learning artifact
text.description: Prepare evidence of a skill, a portfolio, or another artifact that demonstrates learning.

text.label: Set a learning goal and plan a path
text.description: Choose a learning goal and sequence or plan; this activity is distinct from recording focus time as an outcome.

text.label: Attend a class or lesson
text.description: Take part in a class, lesson, lecture, or seminar.

text.label: Practice coding to build a skill
text.description: Complete a coding exercise or lab for the purpose of learning a skill.

text.label: Work through a course
text.description: Complete course materials and assignments according to the course plan.

text.label: Discuss a topic to learn about it
aliases: Discuss a topic in a study group
text.description: Discuss a subject in a group or forum with the aim of learning.

text.label: Drill a learning skill
text.description: Repeat formulas, problems, symbols, patterns, or other skills until they become more automatic.

text.label: Explain an idea to check understanding
aliases: Teach an idea to check understanding
text.description: Explain an idea to yourself or someone else to test whether you understand it.

text.label: Study with focused attention
text.description: Study a subject independently and with concentration, work through material, or practice a skill.

text.label: Complete assigned study work
text.description: Work on an assignment intended for independent completion outside class.

text.label: Listen to an educational podcast or audio lesson
text.description: Listen to a podcast or audio lesson for learning.

text.label: Learn by working on a project
aliases: Solve a problem to practice a skill
text.description: Use your own project or a problem-solving task as a way to learn.

text.label: Continue professional education
text.description: Pursue further education, build professional skills, or take part in continuing professional development.

text.label: Practice recall without prompts
text.description: Retrieve material from memory without cues, such as through flashcards or active-recall exercises.

text.label: Research a learning question
text.description: Explore a study question by finding, comparing, and analyzing materials or making your own observations.

text.label: Study a topic independently using sources
text.description: Explore a question or topic on your own through sources, without following a formal program.

text.label: Take a self-test and review mistakes
text.description: Complete a practice test or self-assessment and analyze mistakes.

text.label: Solve problems to learn
text.description: Solve academic, contest, or practical problems as a learning activity.

text.label: Review material at spaced intervals
text.description: Do spaced repetition or another planned review.

text.label: Take part in a study group
text.description: Learn with a study group, learning group, or co-learning partner.

text.label: Take notes to help remember material
text.description: Create notes, an outline, or a summary of material to support memory.

text.label: Follow a tutorial step by step
text.description: Work through a lesson or workshop by repeating its steps.

text.label: Watch a lecture or instructional lesson
text.description: Watch a lecture, demonstration, or educational course.

text.label: Provide legal advice or prepare a legal opinion
text.description: Advise on a legal matter or prepare a legal opinion; the substance of the advice does not need to be recorded for time tracking.

text.label: Analyze a legal case
text.description: Analyze facts, rules, and evidence as part of a legal role.

text.label: Draft or review legal documents
aliases: Draft or review a legal document
text.description: Draft, edit, or review a contract, filing, response, opinion, or other legal document.

text.label: Conduct legal client intake
aliases: Identify the issue and needed documents
text.description: Receive an inquiry and establish the issue, status, and materials needed.

text.label: Manage case and filing deadlines
text.description: Maintain the calendar for cases, filings, hearings, and responses.

text.label: Negotiate or mediate a dispute or agreement
text.description: Conduct negotiation or mediation about a dispute or the terms of an agreement.

text.label: Organize case materials
text.description: Organize evidence, documents, case files, citations, and timelines.

text.label: Prepare and file official legal documents
text.description: Prepare and submit official documents, and check deadlines and completeness.

text.label: Represent a party at a hearing
aliases: Prepare for or attend a hearing
Present a position at a hearing
text.description: Prepare for or take part in a hearing, present a position, or record the proceedings.

text.label: Research legal sources and case records
text.description: Find and verify applicable law, decisions, records, and case materials.

text.label: Play a game
text.description: Play a chosen game for leisure, alone or with other participants.

text.label: Spend time on another hobby
text.description: Pursue a personal interest that does not have a more specific matching category.

text.label: Take a walk for enjoyment
text.description: Walk for pleasure or relaxation, without a required destination or exercise goal.

text.label: Spend time relaxing or being entertained
text.description: Take part in a chosen leisure or entertainment activity without specifying a more detailed activity.

text.label: Rest quietly while awake
text.description: Take quiet, unstructured rest while awake, without a specific task or entertainment program.

text.label: Model or sculpt a 3D form digitally
text.description: Create or edit a three-dimensional digital form using vertices or digital sculpting. CAD design to exact dimensions and preparing a finished model for printing are related but separate tasks.

text.label: Shoot analog photographs
text.description: Photograph on film to produce exposed frames for later chemical processing or scanning; the defining feature is the analog photographic process.

text.label: Create animation or stop motion
text.description: Create the illusion of movement by capturing successive frames of a drawing, object, or digital form. Stop-motion involves filming an object in stages; computer animation can be fully digital.

text.label: Take photographs
text.description: Choose a frame and capture still photos with a camera or phone. Developing, retouching, selecting, and publishing are separate stages.

text.label: Edit photographs
text.description: Select and edit existing digital images by cropping, adjusting tone or color, retouching, or compositing. Taking photos and publishing them are separate activities.

text.label: Create graphic design or a poster
text.description: Arrange type, images, and shapes to communicate a visual message or make a poster. Unlike drawing, the result usually serves a communication or layout purpose.

text.label: Create an illustration
text.description: Create an image that explains, accompanies, or visually tells a story about a text or idea. Its purpose is tied to specific material, unlike a free-form sketch.

text.label: Practice calligraphy or lettering
text.description: Create decorative letters and inscriptions with controlled pen, brush, or digital strokes. Lettering usually draws the letterforms; calligraphy builds them through a written stroke technique.

text.label: Make a collage or scrapbook
text.description: Compose an image from cutouts, photographs, paper, or other ready-made elements. Scrapbooking adds captions or keepsakes to an album; a collage can stand alone.

text.label: Create a comic or manga
text.description: Develop and create a sequence of illustrated panels with text for a comic or manga. Story writing, drawing pages, and publishing may be phases of one project.

text.label: Edit or color-grade video
text.description: Select, arrange, and join recorded video and audio clips into a sequence, then adjust color if needed. This is assembling recorded material, not filming it.

text.label: Make a print or screen print
text.description: Prepare a printing plate or stencil and transfer an image from it onto paper or another material. Carving the plate and making print runs are related but distinct phases.

text.label: Develop film or print photographs
text.description: Develop exposed photographic film and/or print a photograph from a negative or digital file onto paper. This is laboratory processing, not taking the photograph.

text.label: Draw or sketch
text.description: Draw by hand with lines or strokes, or make a quick sketch, to depict something observed or imagined. The work does not need to be finished.

text.label: Create digital drawing or digital art
text.description: Create a drawing or painted image with digital brushes or layers on a computer or tablet. Do not treat it as graphic design unless the task is to lay out a message or design.

text.label: Film video
text.description: Capture moving images with a camera, choosing framing, movement, and sound. Editing footage that has already been recorded is a separate operation.

text.label: Paint
text.description: Apply pigment to a surface with a brush, palette knife, or another painting method, developing color, tone, and composition. Digital painting can be tracked separately.

text.label: Do woodworking or carpentry
text.description: Make a wooden object or joint by marking, sawing or planing, drilling, and assembling parts. Furniture joinery differs from turning a rotating workpiece on a lathe.

text.label: Make leather goods
text.description: Cut, punch, sew or fasten, and finish leather to make an item. Shoe repair, making an accessory, and tooling are distinct project types.

text.label: Make props
aliases: Make a stage or film prop
text.description: Build a prop for a costume, film shoot, or stage production from chosen materials. Wearing or using the prop and staging a scene are separate activities.

text.label: Make candles, soap, or paper
text.description: This category covers three crafts: pour or shape a candle with a wick, make soap from a base or ingredients, or produce a sheet of handmade paper. Specify the process when possible; these are not one technique.

text.label: Make a sculpture or sculpted form
text.description: Create a three-dimensional sculptural form by adding or modeling material, carving, assembling parts, or combining methods. Clay and other pliable materials are one approach, not the whole of sculpture.

text.label: Make models or miniatures
text.description: Create a scale model or miniature object to represent a space, scene, or design. Game miniatures may also be used in wargaming, but assembling them is still a craft activity.

text.label: Do metalworking or blacksmithing
text.description: Shape or work metal by cutting, joining, forging, or heating. Blacksmithing, which involves hammering heated stock, is one technique within the broader craft of metalworking.

text.label: Build scale models or dioramas
text.description: Assemble a scale model or diorama from a kit or parts, fitting and painting them to represent an object or scene. Assembly and painting may be separate project stages.

text.label: Make a mosaic
text.description: Arrange small tiles, pieces of glass, or stone into an image or pattern and attach them to a base. Cutting pieces and grouting may be stages of the project.

text.label: Do origami or paper craft
text.description: Fold paper along creases to make a figure (origami), or cut, glue, or assemble paper into an object (paper craft); these methods are not interchangeable.

text.label: Bind books
text.description: Sew or glue sheets into a book block and make or attach a cover. Repairing an existing binding and making a new book are related variations.

text.label: Restore furniture
text.description: Stabilize and restore existing furniture by repairing joints or damage, removing old finishes, and refinishing it. Making new furniture is a separate goal.

text.label: Assemble or paint models and miniatures
text.description: Assemble a model or miniature from ready-made parts, paint it, or do both as part of a project. Assembly and painting are distinct operations; designing or playing with the finished miniature are different activities.

text.label: Work with glass or make stained glass
text.description: Cut, assemble, and join colored glass pieces, or shape glass into a decorative object. Stained-glass assembly with seams differs from glass fusing or glassblowing.

text.label: Turn wood on a lathe
text.description: Secure a wooden blank on a lathe and remove material with a cutting tool while it rotates to form a symmetrical piece. This is not a general term for all woodworking.

text.label: Carve or cut a design
text.description: Remove material with a chisel or knife to carve a pattern or three-dimensional form in wood, linoleum, stone, or another material. Specify the material and result separately.

text.label: Make jewelry or beadwork
text.description: Make jewelry from metal, wire, stones, findings, or beads, or create beadwork and patterns that are not jewelry. Specify the technique, such as stringing, weaving, embroidery, or setting.

text.label: Do pottery or ceramics
text.description: Shape a clay object by hand or on a pottery wheel, then optionally dry, fire, and glaze it. A full ceramic project may span several sessions.

text.label: Make a costume or cosplay outfit
text.description: Design and assemble a costume or character outfit through sewing, pattern work, or crafting. Wearing it, taking photos, and role-play are separate activities.

text.label: Do cross-stitch
text.description: Embroider a design with repeated diagonal cross-shaped stitches on canvas or even-weave fabric. This differs from free-form satin stitch and embroidery on a preprinted design.

text.label: Make lace
text.description: Create openwork fabric by interlacing threads into patterns, for example with bobbins or a needle. This differs from knitting dense loops.

text.label: Do quilting or patchwork
text.description: A quilt project may include patchwork piecing (sewing a top from fabric pieces) and quilting (stitching the top, batting, and backing together). You can combine both stages in one personal entry or track them separately.

text.label: Sew patchwork
text.description: Cut and sew fabric pieces into a new cloth or item. Unlike quilting, patchwork alone does not require stitching together the layers of a quilt.

text.label: Make macramé
text.description: Create a pattern or object by tying knots in cord or thread, rather than sewing with a needle or knitting.

text.label: Do needlepoint or weave a tapestry
text.description: This textile category covers two scopes: (1) needlepoint, filling canvas with stitches to create an image; and (2) making a tapestry, which may be woven on a loom or frame. Keep the embroidered and woven practices distinct; “tapestry” is not limited to embroidery.

text.label: Dye yarn or fabric
text.description: Color yarn or fabric using a chosen dye application and setting method. The result is a change in the material’s color, not weaving or sewing it.

text.label: Spin fibers into yarn
text.description: Draw out and twist fibers into continuous yarn by hand or with a spindle or spinning wheel. Dyeing the yarn and knitting or weaving with it are later or separate activities.

text.label: Sew clothing
text.description: Take measurements, cut fabric, and sew pieces together to make clothing. Altering or repairing an existing garment may be tracked as a separate goal.

text.label: Make a fabric doll or stuffed toy
text.description: Cut and sew or stuff fabric to make a doll or soft toy. Pattern drafting, an embroidered face, clothing, and finishing are project stages or facets.

text.label: Weave fabric
text.description: Interlace lengthwise warp threads with crosswise weft on a loom or frame to form fabric. Spinning produces yarn, not woven cloth.

text.label: Do Tunisian crochet
text.description: Pick up and work a row of loops with a special long hook, usually holding the row’s loops until the pass is complete. This is a distinct crochet technique, not another name for ordinary crochet.

text.label: Make felt or felted items
text.description: Mat wool fibers together through friction and moisture or with a needle to form dense felt. Specify wet felting or needle felting when useful.

text.label: Crochet
text.description: Pull yarn through loops with a hook to form fabric or motifs. The hook-based loops and construction distinguish crochet from knitting with needles.

text.label: Knit with needles
text.description: Work loops on straight or circular needles to make fabric or an item. The technique and row construction differ from crochet.

text.label: Embroider
text.description: Stitch thread through fabric according to a design to create decorative stitches. Specify the material or pattern separately when useful.

text.label: Create or edit a 3D model or CAD design
text.description: Create or change digital 3D geometry through polygon modeling, digital sculpting, or parametric CAD. Precise part design is one important subtype, not the entire scope of 3D modeling. Physically printing the model is a separate stage.

text.label: 3D-print an existing model
text.description: Prepare a printer and make a physical part from an existing digital file. Track creating the 3D model or configuring slicer settings separately if useful.

text.label: Practice amateur radio
text.description: Set up a radio station or antenna and communicate with other amateur radio operators, or experiment with transmitting and receiving. Passive listening to broadcast radio is separate.

text.label: Do CNC, laser, or vinyl cutting
text.description: Prepare a file or configure and run a digital cutting or engraving operation: CNC milling or cutting, laser cutting or engraving, or vinyl cutting on a plotter. The machine, process, and material are distinct attributes.

text.label: Do woodworking as a maker project
text.description: Cut, shape, join, or finish wood for a personal maker project. Do not assume this means home repair or professional carpentry.

text.label: Work on a DIY project
text.description: Independently design, make, modify, or repair an item by hand or with tools. Specify the actual operation if a broad project includes several unlike stages.

text.label: Repair or improve the home
text.description: Repair or improve a home or household infrastructure, for example by painting, fixing a finish, or installing a fixture. The goal is home maintenance even when hobby tools are used.

text.label: Build electronics or solder a circuit
text.description: Design or assemble an electronic circuit by mounting components on a circuit or prototyping board and soldering when needed. Programming a microcontroller may be a separate stage.

text.label: Customize a personal vehicle as a hobby
text.description: Change the appearance or configuration of a personal vehicle, such as its parts, paint, interior, or equipment, as a project. Routine repair to restore function is a neighboring but different goal.

text.label: Work with microcontrollers
text.description: Connect and program a microcontroller to read sensors or control devices. Basic circuit soldering and a full robotics project may be neighboring tasks.

text.label: Prepare a slicer or run a 3D print
text.description: Prepare a digital 3D model for printing by orienting it, slicing it, or setting printer parameters; printing can then be started, monitored, or finished separately. Slicing, printer setup, and printing are related but need not all happen together.

text.label: Code as a personal creative activity
text.description: Write, debug, or modify code for a personal project or interest. Work tasks and courses may have a different context; playing a created game is a separate use.

text.label: Develop a game or mod as its creator
text.description: Design rules, levels, or narrative, or code a game or mod. Playing it, testing a build, and publishing are related phases of the creative project.

text.label: Repair a tool or personal item
aliases: Fix a tool or personal belonging
text.description: Diagnose a fault and restore an existing tool or item to working order. Changing its appearance without repairing it may count as customization.

text.label: Build or program a robot
text.description: Assemble and program a robotic device by combining a mechanical structure, sensors, and control. Coding alone or a circuit board alone is a component, not a complete robotics project.

text.label: Assemble furniture
text.description: Assemble a piece of furniture from ready-made parts and hardware using instructions or your own plan. Making parts from scratch and installing the furniture at home are related stages.

text.label: Build or modify a PC
text.description: Assemble, replace, or configure personal-computer components such as the case, boards, cooling, or software. Everyday computer use is not PC assembly.

text.label: Assemble, finish, or paint a model
text.description: Remove supports and seams, sand, assemble, prime, or paint model parts that have already been made. Printing or casting the model itself is an earlier stage.

text.label: Upcycle or repurpose an item
text.description: Turn a used item or material into a new object or function while retaining or reusing the material. Ordinary repair restores its previous purpose.

text.label: Maintain a bicycle
text.description: Clean, lubricate, adjust, diagnose, or replace a bicycle’s consumable parts. Riding the bicycle is a separate activity.

text.label: Work on a maker project
text.description: Plan and build a chosen interdisciplinary prototype or object by combining electronics, mechanics, code, or fabrication. Choose a specific stage instead of this general category when it is known.

text.label: Work on projects in a home lab
text.description: Run a personal experiment or build a prototype at a home-lab workbench. The setting alone does not specify whether the task is measurement, assembly, or analysis.

text.label: Rehearse as an ensemble
text.description: Rehearse a piece together in an instrumental or vocal ensemble, coordinating parts, cues, and tempo before a performance. A public concert is a different stage.

text.label: Arrange music or write it in notation
text.description: This category covers either adapting music for chosen voices or instruments (arranging, with or without writing notation) or recording a musical part or work in notation. The activities may be combined but need not occur together.

text.label: Produce or record audio
text.description: Create audio as a production process: recording a source, programming or editing, assembling tracks, and preparing the project may be stages. Recording sound is one option; mixing and mastering remain separate specialized activities.

text.label: Make beats
text.description: Create rhythmic or musical loops and arrangements with a sampler, drum machine, or DAW. Unlike a DJ set, this involves building material rather than only mixing released recordings.

text.label: Perform a DJ set
text.description: Mix and sequence recordings into a continuous music set, coordinating tempo and transitions. Creating new beats and simply listening to music are different activities.

text.label: Play or practice an instrument
text.description: Play music or practice technique on an instrument. Learning a piece and playing freely may overlap, but tuning or repairing an instrument is a different activity.

text.label: Jam with other musicians
text.description: Improvise and play music with others in a free-form or loosely structured jam. Rehearsing fixed ensemble material involves parts prepared in advance.

text.label: Improvise music or on stage
text.description: Invent and perform material without a fully fixed script or score in advance. This may be stage or musical improvisation; a prepared piece is rehearsed instead.

text.label: Sing karaoke
text.description: Perform a song with a backing track or on-screen lyrics in a karaoke format. This is participation in a playback performance, not necessarily voice training or songwriting.

text.label: Take part in an amateur musical
text.description: Participate in an amateur music-and-theater production combining acting, songs, and choreography. Rehearsing and performing publicly are project phases.

text.label: Master audio
text.description: Prepare a completed mix for release or a medium by adjusting overall level and ensuring the final version translates consistently. This is not multitrack mixing.

text.label: Wear a cosplay costume or portray a character
aliases: Portray a character at a shoot, contest, or role-play event
text.description: Wear a cosplay costume and portray or act as a character. Role-play, photo shoots, contest appearances, and attending a festival may be separate or overlapping episodes. Making the costume and preparing a photo shoot are separate activities.

text.label: Tune or maintain a musical instrument
text.description: Tune an instrument and perform basic care or maintenance, such as changing strings, servicing its mechanism, or cleaning it. Playing music on it is separate.

text.label: Organize an amateur concert or production
text.description: Organize an amateur concert or stage production by coordinating participants, venue and time, program, and practical preparations. Performing on stage and attending as an audience member are separate roles.

text.label: Sing on your own
text.description: Sing alone, perform a song or vocal exercise, or practice your voice. Karaoke adds accompaniment or on-screen lyrics; recording vocals is an additional production task.

text.label: Rehearse stage cues and scene transitions
text.description: Run a production or scene in sequence, coordinating entrances, cues, lighting and sound, transitions, and participants. This is a technical ensemble run-through, not only actors learning lines.

text.label: Perform for an audience or at a home concert
text.description: Perform a music or stage program for an audience, including at a home concert. Attending as an audience member and organizing the event are separate activities.

text.label: Work in a digital audio workstation
text.description: Create or edit a music or sound project in a digital audio workstation (DAW), for example by recording, programming MIDI, or editing clips and plugins. Specify a narrower stage separately if useful.

text.label: Rehearse or sing in a choir
text.description: Sing with a choir while learning a piece or parts at rehearsal, or perform them. Rehearsal is one phase, while public or informal choir singing remains in scope too. Solo singing and watching a choir are different activities.

text.label: Rehearse a dance
text.description: Repeat a dance combination or choreography, practicing timing, steps, formations, and musical accents. Creating new choreography and social dancing are different activities.

text.label: Compose music or a song
text.description: Create new instrumental or vocal music by developing melody, harmony, rhythm, and/or form. A song with lyrics is one kind of composition; instrumental music does not require words.

text.label: Sort or study a record collection
aliases: Study a vinyl and record collection
text.description: Browse, catalog, compare, and explore a music collection or its editions. Listening to a particular recording may happen at the same time, but organizing the collection is its own activity.

text.label: Design sound for a scene or work
text.description: Create or select sound effects and atmospheres for a scene, game, or work by shaping timbre and dynamics. This is not songwriting.

text.label: Perform spoken word or poetry
text.description: Perform a poetic or spoken text aloud in rhythmic delivery for listeners or in rehearsal. Music or a beat may accompany it, but the performance does not have to become a song.

text.label: Write or perform stand-up comedy
text.description: Write or edit jokes, develop a stand-up set, or rehearse or perform it for an audience. Creating comedic material and performing it are related but distinct phases.

text.label: Mix audio tracks
text.description: Balance and process separate tracks to create a combined mix, using levels, panning, equalization, and dynamics. This is not final preparation of the master file.

text.label: Rehearse a theater or acting role
text.description: Rehearse a stage role by working through lines, blocking, intonation, movement, and interactions with scene partners. A technical rehearsal of the scene may be a separate task.

text.label: Translate fan works or fan translations
text.description: Translate a work created in a fandom or a fan translation of another work, carrying its meaning and style into another language. Posting the translation online is a separate stage.

text.label: Write fan fiction
text.description: Create a fictional text in an existing fictional universe or featuring its characters, adding an original plot or scene. Publishing and reading fan fiction are separate activities.

text.label: Write poetry
text.description: Compose or edit poems by choosing words, rhythm, imagery, or form. Reading published poetry and publishing your own work are related but separate activities.

text.label: Write a story or novel
text.description: Write a work of fiction, such as a short story or novel. Reading, editing, and publishing the text are other stages.

text.label: Write a script or game narrative
text.description: Write a story, dialogue, or narrative for an interactive work. Game-mechanics design and programming are related but separate tasks.

text.label: Create an original podcast, vlog, or stream
text.description: Create original online media such as a podcast, vlog, or stream. Planning, recording or hosting live, editing, and publishing may be tracked separately, though they can belong to one production project.

text.label: Create fan art
text.description: Create visual work inspired by characters, a world, or a work from a fandom. Drawing, painting, digital illustration, collage, and other media are possible; this is not by default a text post.

text.label: Create and publish personal creative photos or videos
aliases: Create and publish personal creative photos
text.description: Create and post photos or videos as personal creative work. Editing, filming, and publishing may be separate project phases.

text.label: Create a webcomic
text.description: Create a sequential comic for web publication by developing episodes or pages, arranging panels, and making images with or without text. Publishing may be part of the project, but a webcomic is not just a regular text post.

text.label: Keep a journal or write an essay
text.description: Write personal journal entries or essays. Private journaling, creative writing, and public publication can be distinct activities.

text.label: Write or maintain a personal blog
text.description: Run a personal blog by choosing topics and creating or posting entries or updates in your own authored feed. It may be text, photo, video, or mixed media; reading someone else’s blog is a different activity.

text.label: Build, sort, catalog, or study a collection
text.description: Work with a personal or themed collection: find or acquire items, sort or arrange them, catalog them, take them apart or maintain them, or study the collection. A session may involve one or several of these practices; merely owning a collection is not an activity.

text.label: Attend or watch a live cultural performance
text.description: Be in the audience to watch or listen to live theater, dance, a concert, or another cultural performance. Playing, singing, dancing on stage, and rehearsing are participant activities.

text.label: Visit an archaeological or religious heritage site
text.description: Visit and view an archaeological site or a religious or cultural heritage site. The focus is the site or monument; a ritual or worship service is not implied.

text.label: Visit a library
text.description: Go to a library to use its collection, space, or services: find, borrow, or return materials, work at a desk, or attend an event. Reading a book there is a separate concurrent practice.

text.label: Take a guided tour of a landmark
text.description: Take part in a guided account and follow a route around a landmark or complex. Viewing the site may happen at the same time, but traveling there independently is a separate stage.

text.label: Visit a historic site or monument
text.description: View a preserved historic site or monument in person, such as an architectural or memorial site. Attending a religious service or taking a guided tour are other layers of a visit.

text.label: Visit an art gallery
text.description: Go to an art gallery to view displayed visual works or a curated exhibition. This is an art-display venue or format and does not necessarily mean a museum collection.

text.label: Attend a book festival or book fair
text.description: Attend a public book festival or fair for author events, readings, discussions, or browsing exhibitor stands. Buying books and reading are separate activities; a book fair is not the same as an entertainment fair.

text.label: Visit a museum
text.description: Visit a museum to view its permanent collection, temporary exhibitions, or other displays. The subject and whether there is a tour are details of the visit, not limits on the kinds of exhibits.

text.label: Visit an exhibition or biennial
text.description: View a temporary exhibition or biennial as a visitor, moving among selected works and sections. The event may be held in a museum, gallery, or another venue.

text.label: Walk an architectural route
text.description: Walk along a chosen urban architecture route, viewing buildings or spaces; a guide is optional. An architectural walk combines walking and viewing, which may receive overlapping tags.

text.label: Visit an amusement park, fair, or circus venue
text.description: Enter an amusement park, fair, or circus venue as a guest for leisure. A ride, a purchase, or watching a particular show may be tracked as a distinct activity.

text.label: Visit a zoo, aquarium, botanical garden, or flower show
text.description: Visit a zoo, aquarium, botanical or safari park, or flower show to view organized collections or displays. Searching for a species in the wild is a different activity.

text.label: Attend an amateur match or competition
text.description: Attend a local or amateur match or competition as a spectator and watch participants at the venue. This entry emphasizes a grassroots or local event, not viewing on a screen.

text.label: Watch a motorsport race in person
text.description: Watch a motorsport race as a spectator at the track or viewing area. Spectating is not driving the vehicle or watching an online broadcast.

text.label: Watch a sports competition in person
text.description: Be at the venue as a spectator and watch a live sports competition. Watching a home or online broadcast and taking part as an athlete are different activities.

text.label: Play a game with miniatures
text.description: Use and move miniature figures to act out a scene in a chosen game or an imagined scenario, assigning them roles. If you use a battle-system ruleset, it is a wargame; without one, it is freeform play.

text.label: Play a collectible or trading card game
text.description: Play a collectible card game using a personal deck assembled before the match from cards acquired or traded outside it. This is deck construction and play, not a card market or collecting as a separate activity.

text.label: Play a deck-building game
text.description: Play a deck-builder that starts with a small shared or starter deck and lets players acquire or add cards during the game. This differs from a TCG, where a personal collectible deck is usually built before play.

text.label: Play dominoes
text.description: Play dominoes by matching suitable ends or building a chain according to the chosen variant’s rules. Collecting domino tiles is a separate activity.

text.label: Play Go
text.description: Play Go by placing stones on grid intersections and surrounding territory or an opponent’s stones. Playing a game and independently studying Go problems are distinct activities.

text.label: Play a social deduction or Mafia game
text.description: Take part in a hidden-team game by discussing suspicions and voting or acting to identify secret roles. Discussion-based deduction distinguishes it from games where every role is public.

text.label: Play a card game
text.description: Play a game in which cards are the main components: draw, play or discard cards, or collect combinations according to the rules. Specify a narrower subgenre separately.

text.label: Play a Living Card Game
text.description: Play a Living Card Game (LCG): build a deck from fixed products and play an encounter or scenario. Random collectible booster packs are not the basis for expansion in this model.

text.label: Play tabletop mahjong
text.description: Play tabletop mahjong by drawing and discarding tiles to form a valid winning hand. This is not Mahjong Solitaire, which matches pairs.

text.label: Play a miniature skirmish game
text.description: Play a skirmish scenario with a small squad or individual fighters, emphasizing individual movement, cover, and small-scale conflict. This is a wargame subgenre, not every game that uses miniatures.

text.label: Play backgammon
text.description: Play backgammon by rolling dice, moving checkers along points, and bearing them off according to the rules of the short or long version. Random rolls affect the available moves.

text.label: Play a tabletop game
text.description: Play a tabletop game by taking turns making moves or decisions with components under the rules of one game. This is a broad category; specify the title, genre, and player count separately when useful.

text.label: Play a tabletop role-playing game
text.description: Take part as a player in a tabletop RPG by describing a character’s actions and making decisions in a shared imagined situation with a game master or rules. Scenario preparation and the GM role are separate aspects.

text.label: Play a party game
text.description: Play a short social game for a group, with simple, quickly explained prompts, votes, or team rounds. “Party” describes the audience format, not a single game mechanic.

text.label: Play chess
text.description: Play a chess game by taking turns moving pieces on a checkered board to checkmate the king. Analyzing a game, learning moves, and watching a match are different activities.

text.label: Play a trick-taking card game
text.description: Play a trick-taking game in which participants play one card each into a trick, and rank or trump suit determines who takes it. Scoring depends on the game’s rules.

text.label: Play a miniature wargame
text.description: Play a miniature wargame by moving unit figures across a battlefield or terrain and resolving combat and objectives under scenario rules. The miniatures are game pieces; assembling or painting them is separate.

text.label: Play a historical wargame
text.description: Play out a military-history scenario with models or tokens, using rules for the forces, era, and course of battle. The historical period or battle is the game’s theme, not a separate sport.

text.label: Play a role-playing game by post
text.description: Play a character and advance a role-playing story through messages or posts, with pauses between turns. The asynchronous format differs from a real-time game session.

text.label: Take part in a live-action role-playing game
aliases: Take part in a live-action game
text.description: Take part in a live-action role-playing game by embodying a character and acting or interacting with others in a physical space under agreed rules and a scenario. Cosplay without role-play is not by itself LARP.

text.label: Run a tabletop RPG as the game master
aliases: Run a tabletop RPG as GM
text.description: Run a tabletop role-playing session as the game master by describing the setting, running NPCs and the scenario, and adjudicating the group’s actions under the rules. This is the GM role, not that of a player character.

text.label: Play with toys
text.description: Act out a story or freely interact with toys or figures, assigning roles and actions. Assembling a model or construction set may be a related creative phase.

text.label: Play with LEGO or a construction set
text.description: Build, rebuild, or use LEGO or another construction set in free play. An engineering build designed to perform a specified function may be a separate activity.

text.label: Play a word game
text.description: Play a game whose success depends on inventing, forming, or guessing words, such as word chains or associations, in turns or against a timer. Reading a word puzzle is a different format.

text.label: Play solitaire
text.description: Lay out and move cards for one player according to set rules, aiming to build sequences or foundation piles. It remains a solo game even when played digitally.

text.label: Solve puzzles from a book
text.description: Solve puzzles printed in a book by reading the clues and writing down or checking an answer. The book is the medium; crossword and logic puzzles are possible puzzle types.

text.label: Solve a puzzle in an app
text.description: Interact with a puzzle in an app and check solutions on a screen or by touch. The phone is the platform; the puzzle type defines the logical goal.

text.label: Solve a crossword
text.description: Fill intersecting squares with words using written clues and letters already revealed. Solving word clues is the defining mechanism of a crossword.

text.label: Solve logic puzzles
text.description: Derive a solution from a puzzle’s conditions or constraints by eliminating impossible options. Specify a particular logic-puzzle type separately if useful.

text.label: Solve an arrowword puzzle
text.description: Solve a puzzle by reading short clues placed inside the grid and entering words in the indicated direction. Unlike a standard crossword, its clues are embedded in the grid.

text.label: Solve Sudoku
text.description: Fill a grid with digits or symbols without repeating them in the rows, columns, or specified blocks. This is a logical-constraint puzzle, not arithmetic calculation.

text.label: Solve a logic problem
text.description: Answer a logic problem from text or a diagram by drawing conclusions from its conditions. This is solving a posed problem, not a competitive game.

text.label: Solve a Rubik’s Cube or speedcube
text.description: Turn the faces of a twisty puzzle, such as a Rubik’s Cube, to restore the target color arrangement. Speedcubing is a distinct timed-solving format, not every relaxed solve.

text.label: Assemble a jigsaw puzzle
text.description: Match pieces by shape and image to form one flat picture, usually without turns or competition. A three-dimensional mechanical puzzle works differently.

text.label: Assemble a three-dimensional construction puzzle
text.description: Build a three-dimensional or mechanical construction puzzle from interlocking pieces by shape or instructions until it forms a stable model. This is not assembling a flat jigsaw picture.

text.label: Play a co-op or party video game
text.description: Play a cooperative video game or a video game designed for a group with others. Specify cooperative mode or party format separately when useful.

text.label: Play a fitness or dance game
text.description: Play a game where dance moves or exercises are recognized as input and affect score or progress. Physical exercise may also be a separate meaning for the same time interval.

text.label: Play a puzzle video game
text.description: Play a digital game whose progress requires solving embedded spatial or logic puzzles. Track the platform or title separately; do not conflate it with a paper puzzle.

text.label: Play an interactive novel
text.description: Read and choose branches in an interactive narrative, making decisions that change the story’s course or ending. This is narrative interactivity, not watching a video or reading an unchanged novel.

text.label: Play a computer game
text.description: Control an interactive game on a computer using a chosen input method. PC identifies the platform; genre and online, co-op, or PvP mode are separate dimensions.

text.label: Play a console game
text.description: Play on a home or handheld game console with a controller or other standard input. Genre, solo or online mode, and service are separate details.

text.label: Play a mobile game
text.description: Play a digital game on a phone or tablet using touch or buttons. Mobile describes the device, not a genre or a requirement that sessions be short.

text.label: Play a digital version of a tabletop game
text.description: Play a round of a digital implementation of a particular tabletop game, making moves on screen or online. The tabletop game’s mechanics remain, but physical components are absent.

text.label: Play a cloud or streamed game
text.description: Play through a cloud gaming stream: commands come from the user’s device while the remote computer’s image and processing are delivered over the network. This describes access or delivery, not a game genre.

text.label: Play a solo or online video game
text.description: Play a solo or online video game, alone, together with others, or against other players.

text.label: Play an online RPG or MMORPG
text.description: Play an online RPG or MMORPG by controlling a character, completing quests, fighting, or exploring a persistent shared virtual world with other participants. Social play does not necessarily mean PvP.

text.label: Play a simulation game
text.description: Control a virtual system, machine, or process modeled with its own constraints, such as flight, transport, or farming. “Simulator” describes resemblance to a system, not a training or certification goal.

text.label: Play a VR or XR game
text.description: Play an interactive VR or XR environment by controlling a character or objects through a headset and controller or gestures. VR or XR describes presence and interface, not a game genre by itself.

text.label: Compete in an esports match or tournament
text.description: Play as a participant in an organized esports match, league, or tournament under its rules and compete for a result. Watching a tournament, a practice session, and organizing a team are separate activities.

text.label: Play a slot machine
text.description: Spin or start a slot machine and place a wager to receive a random combination or payout. A digital game with no real money and an arcade game machine may be separate cases.

text.label: Play casino games
text.description: Play a casino game under its probability-based rules, with or without a money wager or prize, such as a table game. Specify the game mechanics (roulette, blackjack, etc.) and stake separately.

text.label: Take part in a lottery or prize draw
aliases: Take part in a prize draw
text.description: Buy a ticket, register, or choose a number in a lottery and wait for a random prize draw. Without a money stake, it may be a free promotional draw rather than gambling.

text.label: Gamble online
text.description: Take part over the internet in gambling or a wager involving money or value. This is a channel for different forms of gambling, not a distinct game mechanic; clarify whether real stakes are involved.

text.label: Play poker for money or in a tournament
text.description: Play a poker game or tournament with money stakes or a prize pool, making decisions about hidden cards, bets, and community cards. Poker as a no-stakes hobby or strategy study is a separate case.

text.label: Bet on sports or horse racing
text.description: Choose an outcome in a sports event or horse race and place a wager, then check the result or settlement. The sporting event itself and watching a race are not betting.

text.label: Read or browse forum discussions
text.description: Browse forum threads and replies to follow the discussion. Reading a particular post or writing a reply is separate participation.

text.label: Scroll through short videos or a social feed
text.description: Scroll through a personalized feed of short videos or posts, moving between items without selecting one specific piece. Stopping to watch an individual video may be a separate activity.

text.label: Browse websites casually
text.description: Move between pages or sites out of curiosity without one preselected article. Purposefully reading a page or searching for a practical answer is different.

text.label: Plan what to watch
text.description: Choose a future movie or video, time, or viewing companions. This is planning, not watching the content itself.

text.label: Browse a streaming catalog
text.description: Search and compare titles in a service catalog to choose something to watch or listen to later. Playback of the selected work has not started.

text.label: Listen to an audiobook
text.description: Listen to a narrated book, in full or in excerpts. Audio is not the same as reading with your eyes, though it may happen alongside another activity.

text.label: Listen to an audio drama
text.description: Listen to a dramatized audio work whose story is conveyed through voices, effects, and sound. This differs from reading a play or watching an adaptation.

text.label: Listen to ambient sound or a recording
text.description: Listen to a soundscape or ambient composition as audio content. Playback device and relaxation goal are session attributes.

text.label: Listen to music, an album, or a playlist
text.description: Listen to a music recording, album, or playlist. A live performance, playing an instrument, and dancing to it may be concurrent but distinct tags.

text.label: Listen to a podcast
text.description: Listen to an audio podcast episode. Hosting or producing the episode and watching a video version are different activities.

text.label: Listen to the radio
text.description: Listen to live radio broadcasting or a recording of it. The station, receiver, or app is the source or means.

text.label: Listen to a talk or lecture for leisure
aliases: Listen to a lecture for leisure
text.description: Listen to an oral presentation or lecture in free time. Whether it is a study or work obligation depends on context and is not required.

text.label: Listen to a live audio stream or room
aliases: Listen to a live audio stream
text.description: Join a live audio room or voice stream as a listener. Speaking through a microphone and hosting the broadcast may be separate or simultaneous activities.

text.label: Read in a library
text.description: Read a chosen text while at a library. “Library reading” describes the place or context; reading and visiting the library can be tracked separately or at the same time.

text.label: Read a blog or website
text.description: Read a selected post, page, or article on a blog or website. Browsing a feed and moving between different items may be a separate practice; the source does not imply a reading purpose.

text.label: Read a long report
text.description: Read an extended analytical or technical report or document, focusing on its text. Work or study obligation may change the context, not the activity.

text.label: Read an ebook
text.description: Read a book on an e-reader or tablet screen. The device and digital medium describe access format, not the text’s genre.

text.label: Read fan fiction
text.description: Read fan-authored fiction based on someone else’s universe or characters. The work is the object; reading is the activity.

text.label: Read a forum or social media post
text.description: Read a selected message, post, or discussion on a forum or social network. Writing a reply and moving between posts are separate activities; the user’s reason for reading is not inferred.

text.label: Read a book, novel, or poetry
text.description: Read an extended, continuous text such as a book, novel, or poetry collection. The precise genre and medium describe content or format, not a separate physical activity.

text.label: Read a comic, manga, or graphic novel
text.description: Read a sequential story combining images and words, moving through panels or pages. This differs from watching an adaptation or looking at standalone images.

text.label: Read the news
text.description: Read written news reports or articles about current events. A video segment or radio broadcast is a different channel.

text.label: Read a newsletter or mailing
text.description: Read a periodic or one-time email newsletter or bulletin. Processing work email is a different context, though it uses the same channel.

text.label: Read an article
text.description: Read one complete piece or article in print or digital form. Viewing an entire page without selecting a text is browsing.

text.label: Read a magazine or newspaper
text.description: Read an issue of a periodical containing a selection of articles or news. Newspapers and magazines differ in editorial format, not in the basic act of reading.

text.label: Watch animation or anime
text.description: Watch an animated film or episode, including anime. Technique or genre describes the work, not a live performance.

text.label: Watch a film or movie
text.description: Watch a film or other cinematic work of any length on a screen at home, in a theater, or while traveling. Viewing location and cinema event are context, not limits on length.

text.label: Watch gameplay or a Let’s Play video
text.description: Watch a recorded video-game playthrough or commentary without controlling the character yourself. Playing interactively and watching a game stream are different modes of participation.

text.label: Watch an esports broadcast
text.description: Watch a live or recorded video-game competition as a spectator. Playing the same game is not the same as watching a match.

text.label: Watch online or short videos
text.description: Watch one or more selected online videos, including short videos. Scrolling through a feed between videos may be tagged as a separate interaction mode; no viewing purpose or lack of purpose is implied.

text.label: Watch a series or episode
text.description: Watch one or more episodes of a series that continues across installments. The title and platform are the content and source.

text.label: Watch a sports broadcast
text.description: Watch a broadcast of a sports match or competition on a screen. Attending in person as a spectator and taking part in the sport are other activities.

text.label: Watch a livestream
text.description: Watch a live stream or broadcast in real time, possibly with chat. Hosting the stream or playing or performing on air is a creator activity.

text.label: Watch a TV program or reality show
text.description: Watch a television program, reality show, or other formatted episode. Unlike a film, this is a broadcast-format program or series.

text.label: Watch a video podcast
text.description: Watch the video version of a podcast conversation or episode. An audio-only episode is listened to, and producing an episode is a separate activity.

text.label: Watch a recorded lecture or video blog
text.description: Watch a previously recorded lecture or video blog. Watching is the activity; learning purpose, creator intent, and subject matter are separate details.

text.label: Take part in an adventure or multisport race
text.description: Compete in a multidiscipline adventure race with a route or checkpoints and whatever navigation the organizer requires. The course may be marked or may require participants to choose their own route. Race stages, disciplines (often running or trekking, cycling, and paddling), transitions, and team format vary. The whole event and its stages may appear as overlapping time views and should not be added together as separate time.

text.label: Bungee jump
text.description: Jump from a height while attached to an elastic cord that stretches and rebounds. A parachute is not the primary means of descent.

text.label: BASE jump
text.description: Jump from a fixed high structure or cliff with a parachute system that opens after exit. This is not a jump from an aircraft or a bungee jump.

text.label: Hang glide
text.description: Fly a rigid delta wing in a suspended harness and steer by shifting body weight. A rigid frame and weight-shift control distinguish it from paragliding.

text.label: Fly in a hot-air balloon or other balloon
text.description: Fly in the basket of a balloon while the pilot controls altitude and direction with the wind in mind. The envelope may be lifted by hot air or gas, so this category is not limited to hot-air balloons. A passenger sightseeing flight and piloting are different roles.

text.label: Paraglide
text.description: Launch beneath a flexible canopy wing and fly by steering its lines or shifting body position. A paraglider folds and does not have the rigid delta frame of a hang glider.

text.label: Skydive or make a parachute jump
text.description: Make a sport or recreational jump from a suitable aircraft, such as a plane or helicopter, using a chosen deployment method: freefall with manual opening, automatic or static-line opening, or a tandem system. Do not imply that every jump includes freefall; distinguish this from a BASE jump from a fixed object.

text.label: Zipline or ropes course
text.description: Ride along a tensioned cable on a zipline or progress through a series of ropes-course obstacles. A zipline is one cable crossing; a ropes course is a sequence of platforms or obstacles; a park is the venue.

text.label: Practice ballet or ballet technique
text.description: Practice ballet technique, such as positions, plié, relevé, and barre or center combinations, or perform choreography. A lesson or rehearsal differs from a stage performance.

text.label: Dance ballroom styles
text.description: Perform partnered ballroom dances in standard or Latin technique during training, a social dance, or a competition. The exact dance program and event are optional details.

text.label: Dance Bollywood choreography
text.description: Learn or perform choreography inspired by Indian cinema or popular stage performance, combining gestures and steps. Do not assume one universal Indian traditional style.

text.label: Practice breaking
text.description: Perform breaking by combining toprock, downrock or footwork, freezes, and power moves in a round or practice session. A battle or stage event and individual practice are different contexts.

text.label: Practice jazz dance
text.description: Practice jazz dance through isolations, rhythmic steps or jumps, and choreography in a chosen stage style. Jazz dance is movement, not listening to jazz music.

text.label: Dance hip-hop
text.description: Dance hip-hop choreography or freestyle using groove and selected street-dance styles or moves. Choreography, battles, and open practice are possible formats.

text.label: Create choreography or rehearse a dance combination
text.description: This category preserves both creating choreography (inventing or staging a sequence of movements and choosing music and space) and rehearsing a completed combination (repeating and refining an already defined sequence). These are related but distinct creative and performance phases.

text.label: Dance Latin or social styles such as salsa, bachata, tango, and swing
aliases: Social dance styles: salsa, bachata, tango, swing, West Coast Swing, and lindy hop
text.description: Dance or learn a selected social style, such as salsa, bachata, tango, swing, West Coast Swing, or lindy hop. Each has its own steps and musical tradition; the list does not describe one standard dance.

text.label: Dance folk or traditional styles
text.description: Perform a folk or traditional dance alone or in a group. Specify the region and tradition separately when useful.

text.label: Dance with a partner
text.description: Dance as a pair, coordinating steps, leading, and following to music. Specify a style such as tango, salsa, or ballroom separately; this is not one single genre.

text.label: Practice pole or aerial dance
text.description: Perform dance or acrobatic elements on a vertical pole or an aerial apparatus such as silks, hoop, or trapeze. Pole and aerial forms use different equipment and techniques and may be tracked separately.

text.label: Rehearse a stage scene
text.description: Repeat acting or movement, blocking, and cues for a stage production. Preparing a show differs from the public performance itself and from attending as a spectator.

text.label: Dance socially
text.description: Dance with a partner or group in a relaxed social setting to music, following an agreed style. This is taking part in dance, not a lesson or rehearsal or watching a performance.

text.label: Practice contemporary dance
text.description: Practice contemporary dance through set or improvised choreography and work with weight, floor, impulse, and space. A specific school or performance is not required.

text.label: Do a dance workout or cardio session
text.description: Repeat continuous dance combinations for physical exertion. Distinguish a fitness or cardio class from a social dance event or stage rehearsal.

text.label: Tap dance
text.description: Create rhythmic patterns with steps in shoes fitted with metal taps, striking the floor to make sound. Dancing and a separate music recording are different activities.

text.label: Practice aikido
text.description: Practice aikido through partner drills on entering, balance, throws, and joint-control techniques. The chosen school or practice determines technical emphasis and contact level.

text.label: Box
text.description: Train or take part in a boxing match, using permitted punches with protective gloves. Kicks and wrestling are outside the basic boxing format.

text.label: Practice Greco-Roman wrestling
text.description: Wrestle by throwing or controlling an opponent with holds above the waist. Holds and attacks involving the legs are restricted by the rules, distinguishing it from freestyle wrestling.

text.label: Practice freestyle wrestling
text.description: Practice freestyle wrestling by attacking or defending with holds and takedowns, using arms and legs for attacks or defense under the style’s rules.

text.label: Practice Brazilian jiu-jitsu or grappling
text.description: Train in BJJ by working on grips, control, and submissions, primarily on the ground. Grappling is a broader family of styles and rules, not a synonym for BJJ.

text.label: Practice judo
text.description: Practice judo with throws, holds, and permitted joint locks or chokes depending on the competition category. Its format and rules differ from BJJ.

text.label: Fence
text.description: Fence with a chosen weapon—foil, épée, or sabre—and make touches or strikes under its rules. The weapon type provides further detail.

text.label: Practice capoeira
text.description: Practice capoeira in a roda, combining musical rhythm, evasions, strikes, acrobatic movements, and play with a partner. It is not simply dancing to music.

text.label: Practice karate
text.description: Practice hand and foot strikes, defenses, and forms (kata) in a chosen karate school. Sparring, kata, and basic technique are different forms of the same practice.

text.label: Practice kendo
text.description: Fence with a bamboo shinai while wearing armor and practice stances or striking lines under kendo rules. This is not foil, sabre, or épée fencing.

text.label: Practice kickboxing
text.description: Train punches and kicks in a kickboxing style or ruleset. Whether knees, clinching, and particular target areas are allowed depends on the organization.

text.label: Do contact sparring
text.description: Have a controlled practice bout with a partner under chosen rules and contact level. Technical drills and a competitive fight are different formats.

text.label: Practice kung fu or wushu
text.description: Practice a chosen Chinese martial-arts style or sport wushu: forms, stances, strikes or weapons, or competition routines. The terms cover different schools and are not exact synonyms.

text.label: Practice mixed martial arts
text.description: Train or compete in mixed martial arts, combining striking, wrestling, and ground control under MMA rules. It combines disciplines and is not a synonym for grappling.

text.label: Practice Muay Thai
text.description: Train in Thai boxing with punches, kicks, elbows, knees, and clinch work under Muay Thai rules.

text.label: Practice sambo
text.description: Train in sambo with throws, holds, and submission techniques under the chosen sport or combat rules. Specify the particular sambo format separately.

text.label: Practice taekwondo
text.description: Practice taekwondo, where sport formats place substantial emphasis on kicks as well as stances, blocks, and forms. Specify kyorugi or poomsae rules when relevant.

text.label: Drill sports techniques
text.description: Repeat sports techniques or moves in exercises without requiring a full bout. Specify the discipline and techniques separately; tag sparring only when it is actually happening.

text.label: Do a barre workout
text.description: Perform a workout combination using a ballet barre or an equivalent support, mixing small strength and mobility movements. This does not have to be a classical ballet class.

text.label: Do breathing exercises
text.description: Intentionally practice exercises for breathing rhythm or control. If used as part of yoga, meditation, or singing, an overlapping tag may be retained.

text.label: Do general gymnastics
text.description: Practice basic gymnastics exercises for coordination, flexibility, balance, and strength. No particular competitive discipline is implied.

text.label: Practice yoga
text.description: Do a chosen practice of poses, breathing, and/or focused movement within yoga. No particular style or goal is assumed.

text.label: Do Callanetics
text.description: Perform a series of small, controlled contractions and held poses for muscular endurance or control. No brand or instructor is required.

text.label: Practice mobility or joint range of motion
text.description: Perform controlled movement through joint ranges and work on active mobility. This differs from holding a static stretch.

text.label: Practice Pilates
text.description: Perform a sequence of controlled Pilates exercises for strength, core control, and mobility. Mat or equipment and the style are details.

text.label: Stretch
text.description: Hold or repeat positions and movements to increase the range of motion of muscles or joints. A warm-up or rehabilitation program may be the context but is not implied.

text.label: Practice tai chi or taijiquan
text.description: Practice a chosen form of taijiquan through sequences, transitions, or paired and applied exercises with body control. Pace may be slow or fast depending on the school or format.

text.label: Do a dance workout or dance aerobics
text.description: Repeat choreographed movements for a fitness workout. A dance class or cardio format and social dancing are different possible contexts.

text.label: Practice qigong or kung fu exercises
